issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh shifts, or the van losing drive. Some owners had a rebuilt unit fail again soon after.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears internally. Owners report full transmission failures around 50,000–75,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or won't move, stop driving it hard and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuilt or used unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: StabiliTrak brakes a wheel or pulls the van on its own
issues.sym: The van suddenly brakes one wheel, pulls or swerves, often with a 'Service Stability System' or traction warning, sometimes at highway speed.
issues.why: The stability system reacts to bad data from the yaw rate sensor, the steering wheel position sensor or a front wheel sensor. Owners also found wiring rubbed through near the ABS module. This is the most common complaint to NHTSA for the 2005 Terraza.
issues.next: Have the stability and ABS codes read and the sensors and wiring checked. Some owners needed more than one repair, so make sure the cause is confirmed before paying for parts.

issues.t: Power sliding door won't close, latch or stay shut
issues.sym: A power sliding door stops partway, reverses, won't latch, or opens on its own. Owners report doors opening while driving.
issues.why: The door motor, cable, rollers and latch wear out or go out of adjustment.
issues.next: Lock the doors and don't let passengers lean on a door that isn't latching. A shop can adjust the door or replace the roller, cable, motor or latch.

issues.t: Door-ajar chime won't stop or false door warnings
issues.sym: The door chime keeps ringing or the dash says a door is open when it's closed, which can also affect the dome light and cruise control.
issues.why: The door-ajar switches and sensors in the sliding doors and latches fail or get out of adjustment.
issues.next: Have the door switches and latches checked. Resetting or replacing the sensor usually fixes it.

issues.t: ABS and traction lights from a wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: ABS, traction control or StabiliTrak warning lights stay on.
issues.why: The front wheel speed sensors and their wires fail. On this van the sensor is part of the front hub, so the hub is often replaced.
issues.next: Have the codes read to find which wheel is at fault. The brakes still work normally, but ABS and stability control are off until it's fixed.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum or play
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed, or play in a front wheel that fails inspection.
issues.why: The front hub bearings wear out, often between 55,000 and 170,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked on a lift. Replace a noisy hub before it gets loose.

issues.t: Rear air-leveling shocks fail
issues.sym: The rear sags, the ride gets bouncy, or the leveling system won't hold air.
issues.why: The rear air shocks used for automatic leveling leak or corrode with age.
issues.next: Have the air shocks and lines checked. Many owners convert to standard shocks.

issues.t: Rear trailing arm can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Squeaking or clunking from the rear, then the van feeling loose at the back.
issues.why: The rear trailing arm bushings can wear early, and the arm can crack or separate, which can partly detach the rear axle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 10V110000. If you hear rear clunks, have the arms inspected right away.

issues.t: Parking brake can slip and drag (recall)
issues.sym: Noise from the rear or a feeling that the brakes are dragging after the parking brake is released.
issues.why: The parking brake lever can slip after release, so the rear brakes stay partly on.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V287000. The dealer checks the parking brake and replaces rear calipers if needed.

issues.t: Tire label shows wrong load data (recall)
issues.sym: The tire and loading label on the door jamb shows the wrong weight capacity.
issues.why: A misprinted label could lead owners to overload the van or set the wrong tire pressure.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 05V552000. The dealer replaces the label for free.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from a wet connector under the driver's seat
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving, won't start, or random warning lights come on.
issues.why: A wiring connector under the driver's seat can get wet and corrode. Owners also report engines dying at various speeds.
issues.next: Have the connector under the driver's seat checked for corrosion and water. Fix any leak that gets the floor wet.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The gauge shows fuel when the tank is near empty, or won't read full after filling up.
issues.why: Sulfur deposits corrode the fuel level sender in the tank.
issues.next: Track miles since your last fill-up. A shop can try GM's fuel system cleaner first; if that doesn't work, the sender needs replacing.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed EGR valve
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with rough running.
issues.why: The EGR valve can stick or clog. GM's fix was a replacement valve from another supplier and an engine computer reflash.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Ask a dealer whether the updated valve and software were installed.

issues.t: Whistle under acceleration from the PCV tube
issues.sym: A whistling noise when you accelerate, or a check engine light. The plastic PCV tube may be loose or cracked.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) tube on the 3.5L V6 cracks or comes loose.
issues.next: Replace the PCV tube. It's a small part.

issues.t: Headlights and interior lights flicker
issues.sym: Headlights and interior lights flicker or dim.
issues.why: The alternator's output becomes unsteady, and replacing the alternator is the usual fix.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. A failing alternator can leave you stranded.

issues.t: Dash gauges stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer or other gauges stop working or act strangely.
issues.why: Owners report gauge failures on the 2005 Terraza, pointing to the instrument cluster.
issues.next: Have the cluster tested. Rebuilding the cluster is usually an option instead of a new one.

issues.t: OnStar loses power
issues.sym: OnStar doesn't work or the OnStar lights are off.
issues.why: The communication interface module fails. Pulling the fuse resets it only for a while.
issues.next: OnStar's old analog service has ended, so many owners don't fix this unless it drains the battery.

issues.t: Horn hard to sound
issues.sym: You have to press certain spots on the steering wheel pad hard to make the horn work.
issues.why: The horn pad springs are too stiff. Softer springs are available as a retrofit.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to install the softer springs.

issues.t: Brake pulsation from warped front rotors
issues.sym: A pulsing brake pedal or shaking steering wheel when stopping, sometimes with squeals.
issues.why: Owners report front rotors warping early, sometimes more than once. Uneven lug nut torque can make it worse.
issues.next: Replace pads and rotors together and make sure the shop tightens the wheels with a torque wrench.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends cause looseness or clunks
issues.sym: Clunks, loose steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Owners report tie rod ends wearing out early, sometimes with sway bar bushings.
issues.next: Have the front end checked and get an alignment after any steering part is replaced.

issues.t: Oil and coolant leaks at the front of the engine
issues.sym: Oil or coolant spots under the front, a sweet coolant smell, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: The coolant crossover, timing cover and crankshaft balancer area can leak on this V6.
issues.next: Watch the coolant and oil levels and have the leak found. Running low on coolant can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Oil pan leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine.
issues.why: The oil pan gasket seeps with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the gasket replaced if it drips.

issues.t: Cruise control stops working
issues.sym: Cruise control won't set or cuts out.
issues.why: The cruise control switch on the steering wheel fails. False door or brake signals can also cancel cruise.
issues.next: Have the switch tested and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Shift cable bushing breaks
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the gear doesn't change, or the van won't come out of Park.
issues.why: The small plastic bushing that connects the shift cable to the transmission wears out and falls off.
issues.next: A new bushing fixes it. Set the parking brake until it's repaired.

issues.t: Transmission cooler line leak
issues.sym: Red fluid drips near the front of the van, or shifting gets worse as fluid drops.
issues.why: The metal transmission cooler lines rust or their fittings leak.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and have the lines replaced before the transmission runs low.

issues.t: Check engine light from a stuck-open thermostat
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0128, slow warm-up and weak heat.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks open, or the coolant temperature sensor reads wrong.
issues.next: Replace the thermostat and sensor if needed.

issues.t: Rear wiper stops working
issues.sym: The rear wiper doesn't move.
issues.why: The rear wiper motor fails.
issues.next: Replace the motor. Check the fuse first.
